angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 3,421,453 km at 167.89 pc = 0.27 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82651: distance 167.89 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.046), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 167.89 +/- 7.723 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 6.0800 +/- 0.0198 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03), 307.6 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 4.918 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82651: radius 4.918 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 13.107 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.068) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 3,421,453 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4956 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82651: effective temperature 4956 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 82651: effective temperature 4956 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.04) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 152581 (pscomppars): spectral type K0, from Cannon & Pickering 1918 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1918AnHar..91....1C/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 152581: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 152581 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.46 dex, from Johnson et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..197...26J/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 152581 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.17319, from Johnson et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..197...26J/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 152581 (pscomppars): age 12 Gyr, from Johnson et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..197...26J/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 152581 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.5 km/s, from Johnson et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011ApJS..197...26J/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.28 from 2024A&A...691A..53S; the 8 published values span log g 3 to 3.47, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...691A..53S)
